html_tabs.title: Verified variants
html_tabs.html:
Single-cell resolved variant calling. p2single keeps exact sequences, so it finds variants in individual cells. In THP-1 cells it found the known NRAS G12D variant (c.35G>A, p.Gly12Asp). In a single-cell study of non-small cell lung cancer it found the cancer-driving KRAS G12V mutation (c.35G>T, p.Gly12Val) in 33 cells of one patient: all 17 mutant cells with a cell-type label are tumour epithelial cells, and no other patient has it. A 5′ UTR variant in JAK2 (rs2274472) was also found in 1,968 THP-1 cells, along with variants in hundreds of genes, including COSMIC variants and variants of unknown significance in ClinVar.

html_tabs.title: Mutations vs sequencing noise
html_tabs.html:
Every COSMIC match with a wild-type sequence at the same site in the three studies (390 sites; 92 more have no wild-type sequence in the list, so no share can be computed). Each grey dot is one site; green dots are the named variants. 126 of 390 sites have under 1% mutant reads, the level of sequencing error, mostly in highly expressed genes such as B2M and ACTB. NRAS G12D and KRAS G12V stand far above that level. KRAS G12C and CTNNB1 Y30* are low study-wide because few cells carry them; within their own tumour cells the share is high (first tab). Grey dots high on the chart are mostly common inherited variants; hover a dot to see it.

How the share is computed. For each COSMIC site, the reads of all p2single sequences with the mutant base divided by the reads of the mutant and wild-type sequences at that site, over all cells of the study. Source: s3://rosa-pipeline/outputs/variant-carriers-2026-10-29/ carrier and pair files; THP-1 from the motif carrier file.
